contributions.statement: Never key agent, tool or broker routing on a peer-advertised display name; route by an operator-enrolled, origin-bound ID, keep names presentational, and fail closed on exact or normalisation-equivalent duplicates.
contributions.evidence: Table 1: 6 of 7 pinned frameworks (ADK Python/TS, UiPath, BeeAI, Any-Agent, AutoDev) dispatched A-addressed requests to lower-trust peer B; Solace collapsed both to one route; Table 3: seven negative controls (incl. ADK Java) show the fix works.
relative_to: name-based identity confusion (CWE-706); authenticate identity, do not trust self-asserted names

contributions.statement: When composing tools from several MCP or agent servers, check the host's tool-name collision policy; a default 'warn' policy silently keeps the last colliding tool.
contributions.evidence: §4/Table 1: Any-Agent with OpenAI Agents SDK 0.20.0 default warn policy retained the last colliding function tool; UiPath/BeeAI generated tool names from remote metadata.

reason: Concrete, reproducible wrong-peer dispatch across pinned real frameworks with matched negative controls; directly relevant to any team composing multiple MCP/agent servers.
